clue.text: Children in main go round hunting

parts.note: the main is an old poetic word for the open sea

indicators.note: the children are placed inside the circle, so this word signals containment

parts.note: a ring is a circle, something that goes round

explanation.surface: Kids out at sea on a boat, circling about while hunting for something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Children in main' tempts you to put CH inside the sea word, but the CH actually goes into the ring that follows.
explanation.definitionFit: Searching and hunting are synonyms: both describe looking hard for something.

clue.text: Boat's a runner (very loud)

parts.note: a ski is a runner, the long blade a sledge or skier slides on
FF is fortissimo, the musical marking for very loud

explanation.surface: A boat described as a speedy, noisy machine.
explanation.definitionFit: A skiff is a small light rowing or sailing boat.

clue.text: Skill leading German invader to adopt elevated attitude of British king

indicators.note: the skill word goes in front of the rest, leading it

parts.note: art means skill, as in the art of persuasion

indicators.note: to adopt is to take in, so the invader word holds the next piece inside it

parts.note: Hun is an old, hostile name for a German soldier or invader

indicators.note: in a down clue, elevated means the word is written upwards, bottom to top

parts.note: an air is a manner or attitude, as in an air of superiority

explanation.surface: A skilled German invader adopting a lofty manner in the presence of a British king.
explanation.walkthrough: 'elevated' turns the attitude word upside down in this down entry, and 'to adopt' puts that inside the invader; 'leading' sets the skill word first.
explanation.definitionFit: Arthurian is the adjective for things relating to the legendary British King Arthur.

clue.text: Get to bring in right stuff from fields

indicators.note: bringing something in means holding it inside, so the first word contains the second

parts.note: to cop is slang for to get or receive, as in cop a fine

explanation.surface: An instruction to harvest goods from farmland.
explanation.definitionFit: A crop is the produce grown and harvested from fields.

clue.text: Likely spouse? Interest's not continuing

parts.note: INT is the abbreviation for interest, as in banking
something that has ended is no longer continuing

explanation.surface: Someone muses that a possible marriage partner has lost interest.
explanation.definitionFit: One's intended is the person one plans to marry, a fiancé or fiancée, hence a likely spouse.

clue.text: Deranged fisherman forbidding even parts of nets

parts.note: grim means stern and forbidding in appearance

indicators.note: the even-numbered letters, second and fourth, are taken from the word nets

explanation.surface: A crazed angler with a stern face hauling in his nets.
explanation.walkthrough: Peter Grimes is the disturbed fisherman of Benjamin Britten's opera, the composer at 27 Across.
explanation.definitionFit: Peter Grimes is the troubled, unhinged fisherman who gives his name to Britten's opera.

clue.text: Money is, with little hesitation, near fellow

parts.note: er is the short sound of hesitation in speech

explanation.surface: Someone with money hesitates while standing beside a man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'near' looks like a position, but here it means stingy.
explanation.definitionFit: Near is an old word for stingy, so a near fellow is a tight-fisted hoarder of money.

clue.text: Low luminance in the dark?

parts.note: the faint light seen at night comes from the moon, a dim glow in the darkness

explanation.surface: A technical question about a dim light source at night.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Moonlight' is also one of Britten's Four Sea Interludes, the puzzle's theme.
explanation.definitionFit: The light reflected by the moon is a faint glow, the only brightness on a dark night.

clue.text: Turned up nearly comatose with cut from weapon

indicators.note: in a down clue, turned up means the letters are read from bottom to top
the last letter is cut off the sleepy word

parts.note: drowsy means half asleep, almost unconscious

explanation.surface: Someone turns up half-unconscious with a wound from a weapon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with cut' trims DROWSY to DROWS, which 'Turned up' turns into SWORD.
explanation.definitionFit: A sword is a bladed weapon.

clue.text: They resist misrepresenting hero figures

indicators.note: to misrepresent is to present wrongly, so the letters of hero are put in a different order

parts.note: stats, short for statistics, are figures

explanation.surface: People who refuse to accept distorted figures about a hero.
explanation.walkthrough: 'misrepresenting' rearranges HERO into RHEO.
explanation.definitionFit: Rheostats are variable resistors, electrical devices that resist current.

clue.text: Hymn: keen on it when Rector enters

indicators.note: the rector letter goes into the keen word

parts.note: to be into something is to be keen on it

explanation.surface: A parishioner is fond of a hymn when the rector walks into church.
explanation.definitionFit: An introit is the psalm or hymn sung as the priest enters at the start of a service.

clue.text: Type of atom: is oxygen best to get energy?

parts.note: O is the chemical symbol for oxygen
top means best, as in top marks
E is the symbol for energy in physics

explanation.surface: A chemistry question about whether oxygen is the best source of energy.
explanation.definitionFit: An isotope is one form of an element's atom, differing in its number of neutrons.

clue.text: Number good books, but not Good Book?

definitions.text: Number good books, but not Good Book?

parts.words: Number good books, but not Good Book?
parts.note: the gospels, the books of good news, total this many, though the whole Bible holds far more

explanation.surface: Counting worthy books while leaving out the Bible.
explanation.walkthrough: Gospel means 'good news', so the gospels are the good books; there are four of them, but the Good Book, the Bible, has many more. The number also begins Britten's Four Sea Interludes.
explanation.definitionFit: Matthew, Mark, Luke and John make the gospel count, a small part of scripture.

clue.text: I note playing resulted in short pieces

indicators.note: the letters of resulted are played about with, rearranged

explanation.surface: A musician reports that playing a note produced some brief works.
explanation.walkthrough: 'playing' rearranges RESULTED into TERLUDES.
explanation.definitionFit: Interludes are short pieces of music played between longer sections or acts.

clue.text: River's course doing for South American plant

parts.note: Aintree is a racecourse near Liverpool, home of the Grand National steeplechase

explanation.surface: A river's path serving as home to a tropical plant.
explanation.walkthrough: AINTREE is the English racecourse near Liverpool where the Grand National horse race is run.
explanation.definitionFit: The rain tree is a large tropical tree native to South America.

clue.text: Detective, losing student, tailing all others in certain establishments

indicators.note: to tail is to follow behind, so the detective word comes after the others word

parts.note: the rest means all the others

indicators.note: the student letter is lost from the detective's name

parts.note: Sherlock Holmes is the classic fictional detective
L is for learner, the student driver's plate

explanation.surface: A detective shadowing everyone else inside some institutions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'losing' removes L from HOLMES, leaving HOMES.
explanation.definitionFit: Rest homes are particular kinds of residential establishment for the elderly or convalescent.

clue.text: I put maze in new arrangement, including hint of rectangular shape

indicators.note: the rearranged letters hold the next piece inside them
the letters of I put maze are put in a new order
a hint is a small trace, the first letter only

explanation.surface: Someone redesigning a maze to include a rectangular touch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in new arrangement' turns IPUTMAZE into TAPEZIUM; 'including' slips in R, from 'hint of rectangular'.
explanation.definitionFit: A trapezium is a four-sided geometric shape with one pair of parallel sides.

clue.text: Range about to be terminated — what's to be done?

indicators.note: the range word goes about, around, the next piece

parts.note: an Aga is a British brand of heavy cast-iron kitchen range cooker
to end is to be terminated, come to a stop

explanation.surface: A kitchen range is about to be scrapped, so what now?
explanation.walkthrough: AGA is a British make of range cooker, the big iron stove of a country kitchen.
explanation.definitionFit: An agenda is a list of items to be dealt with, the things to be done.

clue.text: Blast affected tenor's ear

indicators.note: affected means altered, so the letters are changed into a new order

explanation.surface: A loud blast has damaged a singer's hearing.
explanation.definitionFit: A nor'easter is a strong wind or gale blowing from the northeast.

clue.text: Power and energy within range for a start

parts.note: P is the symbol for power in physics

indicators.note: the energy letter goes within the roaming word

parts.note: to range is to roam, to ramble
E is the symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A physics note on power and energy at the start of a scale.
explanation.definitionFit: A preamble is an introduction, the opening statement before the main text.

clue.text: Time at weekend for one to embrace a French date

indicators.note: to embrace is to hold, so the example word holds the next pieces

parts.note: say means for example, for one
un is the French word for a

explanation.surface: Someone at the weekend agrees to embrace a French date.
explanation.definitionFit: Sunday is the last day of the weekend, a time when people rest.

clue.text: Not the Dog-Star — Cur-Star, second in luminosity, possibly

indicators.note: possibly means the letters might be arranged another way
second in means the second letter of the next word

explanation.surface: A star is not Sirius but a 'cur star', ranking second in brightness.
explanation.walkthrough: A cur is a dog, so 'Cur-Star' sounds like the Dog-Star but isn't. 'possibly' rearranges CURSTAR plus U, the second letter of luminosity.
explanation.definitionFit: Arcturus is a bright star in Boötes, distinct from Sirius, which is called the Dog Star.

clue.text: Legal experts mostly fair about daughter, say, when had up

indicators.note: the shortened fair word goes about, around, the rest
mostly means all but the last letter is used

parts.note: just means fair

indicators.note: in a down clue, had up means the letters are written upwards

parts.note: eg, for example, is what say means here

explanation.surface: Lawyers who are mostly fair about a daughter, such as when she was arrested.
explanation.walkthrough: 'had up' is slang for arrested but here turns 'say' upwards in this down entry; 'mostly' drops the last letter of the fair word, and 'about' wraps it round the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Judges are experts in law who preside over courts.

clue.text: Auditorium and oratorio with one vocal change, God be praised

parts.note: a hall is a large room for audiences

indicators.note: one vowel in the oratorio's name is swapped for another

parts.note: Elijah is Mendelssohn's oratorio

explanation.surface: A concert hall staging an oratorio with one vocal part altered, to praise God.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with one vocal change' swaps the I of ELIJAH for U, giving ELUJAH.
explanation.definitionFit: Hallelujah is a Hebrew exclamation meaning 'praise the Lord'.

clue.text: No active movement participating in popular Government

indicators.note: the letters take part in the phrase popular government, sitting within it

explanation.surface: A political party that refuses to join in popular government.
explanation.walkthrough: 'movement' looks political but is a piece of music.
explanation.definitionFit: Largo is a very slow musical movement, far from lively or active.

clue.text: Opening event tied, after runs discounted

indicators.note: the runs letter is discounted, left out

parts.note: a drawn game is one that ended tied
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A cricket match's first fixture ended level once the runs were struck off.
explanation.definitionFit: Dawn is the first light of day, the opening event of every morning.

clue.text: Bar in US city supplying dope

indicators.note: the bar word goes inside the city abbreviation

parts.note: NY is New York
an inn is a pub or bar

explanation.surface: A bar in an American city selling drugs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dope' looks like drugs but means a fool.
explanation.definitionFit: A dope is a fool, and so is a ninny.

clue.text: Angry author of plays on the radio

indicators.note: on the radio means spoken over the air, heard rather than read

parts.note: Oscar Wilde wrote plays such as The Importance of Being Earnest

explanation.surface: A playwright being furious during a radio broadcast.
explanation.definitionFit: Wild can mean furious, extremely angry.

clue.text: Sound of complaint: right to block one out in early part of day

indicators.note: the right letter stands in the way of one letter, blocking it
the blocked letter is pushed out, so one is replaced

parts.note: moaning is the sound people make when complaining
A, the indefinite article, means one

explanation.surface: A grumble about the right to block someone out early in the day.
explanation.walkthrough: R replaces the A in MOANING.
explanation.definitionFit: Morning is the early part of the day, before noon.

clue.text: Composer put pen to paper, displaying book for women

indicators.note: the book letter is put in place of the women letter

parts.note: to put pen to paper is to write, so the past form is written

explanation.surface: A writer produces a women's book.
explanation.walkthrough: Benjamin Britten is the theme composer: his Four Sea Interludes are Dawn, Sunday Morning, Moonlight and Storm.
explanation.definitionFit: Benjamin Britten was a leading twentieth-century English composer.

clue.text: Eminence engaged in kinky sex, provoking outrage

indicators.note: the hill word is engaged, held, inside the other

parts.note: SM is sadomasochism
a tor is a rocky hill, an eminence

explanation.surface: A high figure caught in kinky sex provoking public outrage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Eminence' looks like a cardinal but is a hill; a TOR is a rocky hilltop, as on Dartmoor.
explanation.definitionFit: A storm can mean a violent outburst of public anger, an outcry.

clue.text: Slightly crafty about mortgage provider

indicators.note: the crafty word goes about, around, the lender word

parts.note: sly means crafty
a lender, such as a bank, provides a mortgage

explanation.surface: A crafty mortgage lender.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Slightly' looks like 'a little' but means thinly.
explanation.definitionFit: Slightly can mean in a slight, slim manner, a synonym of slenderly.
